meta.title: Our Nature Park
meta.textType: a descriptive text about a place

paragraphs: Our Nature Park, posted by Mia. The nature park is near our town, and it is a good place for a school trip. The Explorers go there many times in a year. This post describes the park for our readers. The park has a rainforest, a river, and a visitor center. Do you want to know more about it? The air is cool and fresh, and the trees are very tall.

In the forest, you can certainly see many birds. Monkeys sit in the tall trees, and small frogs sit on the leaves. In the morning, the birds are in action. They fly, they sing, and they look for food. The best time to look is early, before the sun is hot. Some animals are hard to see, so please be quiet. A quiet visitor sees more than a loud visitor. A small stream runs through the forest. You can hear water, birds, and insects at the same time.

The visitor center is a big wooden house near the river. Somebody is always at the desk, so you can ask a question. The desk has a big book, and every visitor writes a name in it. Behind the center, there are six small cabins for school groups. This accommodation is simple. Each cabin has four beds, a fan, and a small table. A group can stay for one night. Teacher Kim writes to the ranger before each stay. The center also has a map of the park on the wall.

The rangers wear green caps and strong boots. The boots are made of leather, and they are good for wet ground. Rangers walk in the park every day. They count birds, and they help the visitors. Some rangers also work in the visitor center. Every ranger wears a small name badge.

Here are the directions from our school to the park. First, take the bus to the park gate, and the journey takes forty minutes. Then walk straight on the main path. At the big fig tree, turn left. After that, cross the small bridge. The visitor center is on the right, next to the river. The walk from the gate to the center takes ten minutes. Please stay on the path, and do not touch the animals. Do not forget your water and a hat. Which part of the park do you want to see first?
text.summary: Mia describes the nature park for the readers of Explorers' Blog. She tells about the animals, the visitor center, the cabins for school groups, the rangers, and the directions to get there.
